study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Identify OCD subtypes using individualized deviations from normative models of regional gray matter volume (GMV), test reproducibility, and examine associations with brain network architecture and neurotransmitter receptor/transporter distributions.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Disease epicenter mapping via structural covariance (SC) network predicted from neighboring regional abnormalities; association with PET-derived neurotransmitter receptor/transporter profiles using multilinear models with permutation testing (FDR) and dominance analysis to assess predictor importance.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Identified two robust OCD subtypes with opposite GMV deviation patterns relative to HCs; distinct disease epicenters (subtype 1: middle frontal gyrus; subtype 2: striatum/thalamus/hippocampus) and distinct associations with neurotransmitter receptors (e.g., 5HT1A for subtype 1; 5HT2A for subtype 2).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: K-means clustering on 246-region z-score vectors revealed two subtypes (optimal k=2 by silhouette). Reproducibility: ARI = 0.98 (±0.04) for 90% resamples; consistent subtypes across AAL atlas (ARI=0.74) and correlation distance metric (ARI=0.62). Subtype 1 shows increased GMV in frontal gyrus, precuneus, insula, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, amygdala, temporal gyrus (FDR<0.05); subtype 2 shows decreased GMV in frontal/precuneus/insula/superior parietal/temporal/fusiform (FDR<0.05). Neurotransmitter models: adjusted R^2=0.43 (F(246,226)=10.80) for subtype 1 and 0.34 (F(246,226)=7.76) for subtype 2; all permutation p<0.001 (FDR).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative modeling implemented with GPML 4.2; structural covariance mapping leveraged an external single-site HC dataset (n=492) to define SC network; dominance analysis (Python) used to rank neurotransmitter predictors; group-level voxelwise differences evaluated via SPM12.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Single-site dataset without external validation of the normative model; no reported fit metrics (EV/MSLL) or independent holdout; normative model includes only age and sex predictors; results derived from regional GMV (atlas dependence).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: SC network constructed from an independent single-site HC dataset (n=492, age 19–80) used for disease epicenter analyses, not for normative modeling. Imaging QC via CAT12 IQR; groups matched on TIV and IQR. Acquisition parameters provided for 3T GE MR750.
